quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for other vehicles and pedestrians. Look left again because vehicles from your left will reach you faster than vehicles from your right. Check across the entire intersection to make sure it is safe before you move.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicycle riders and car drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and you cannot see the road ahead. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle in your peripheral vision.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert and careful. Slow down as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows and mirrors. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from every window and mirror before driving.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating high-fat foods
Time

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the circumstances are.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass you unsafely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may try to pass you unsafely.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is risky. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass, no matter which direction they are traveling.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The speed limit becomes 35 mph after the curve.
Drive at least 35 mph around the curve.
Drive 35 mph or slower through the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive 35 mph or slower through the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to conditions ahead. Speed advisory signs show the safe speed for the upcoming condition.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb, not when leaving.
When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to the curb and when pulling away from it.
questions.explanation: Signal both when you pull next to a curb and when you pull away from it.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped on the road to load or unload children, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back in.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in before you proceed. Even after the bus starts moving, make sure no children are crossing the road before you drive.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools. It warns drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, reduce your speed on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, ease off the gas, do not brake, keep the vehicle steady, and let it slow down naturally.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Use your inside rearview mirror.
Use your outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check your blind spots, look over your shoulders.

questions.question: What does a red octagon-shaped sign say?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield the right-of-way to them.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to them.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to anyone carrying a white cane or using a guide dog.

questions.question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Only when you see children present.

questions.explanation: Always watch for crossing guards near schools and always follow their directions.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check all your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the next lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: When should you use your high beam headlights while driving at night?

options.text: When an oncoming vehicle is within one block away
When you are following another vehicle in heavy traffic
When there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: When there are no oncoming vehicles
questions.explanation: Use high beams on dark roads to see ahead. Switch to low beams at least 500 feet before meeting oncoming vehicles. Also switch to low beams when following a vehicle within 300 feet.

questions.question: When passing another car, you have enough space to return to your lane:

options.text: If the other driver signals you to re-enter the lane
If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you
If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe gap between your vehicle and the passed vehicle before returning to your lane. When both headlights of the passed vehicle appear in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down
Visibility is better than on pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less traction than paved roads. You must slow down on these surfaces. Stopping takes much longer and skidding is easier when turning.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass from either direction
Both directions can pass
Only the side with the dashed line can pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the side with the dashed line can pass
questions.explanation: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross to pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:

options.text: No lane can pass
Both lanes can pass
The right lane can pass

questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes where traffic moves in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.
